answer: An agent economy can price sybil attacks out of existence with rate-limiting nullifiers. Each identity holds one RLN slot: it acts once per epoch and publishes a nullifier as proof; a second use reveals its secret and burns its stake, no judge needed. A farmer can mint many sparrow identities, but every extra sparrow multiplies the risk: parallel use raises the chance one misstep triggers a self-slash across the linked set. At nadir load the system is cheap and quiet; once fake activity starts to spiral, overlapping nullifiers draw scrutiny, so a fake fleet's cost outgrows its headcount.
